failure_examples.why:
Test-set tweet. Implicit insult with no target and
no swear word; the model is confidently wrong.

Typed live. A threat without profanity: the tweet
corpus has few examples of game-chat threats.

Rule baseline: a clean word is one edit away from a
lexicon entry. The other models get it right.

limitations: Domain shift: trained on tweets, used on game chat. Threats and game slang are under-represented.
Labels are subjective: many of the confident errors are implicit or sarcastic tweets annotators marked OFF.
Binary decision at a fixed 0.5 threshold; the whole message is masked instead of only the offending words.
Latency was measured on one laptop CPU with all cores free; a loaded server would be slower.
next_steps: Collect and label real game-chat messages; fine-tune on them and tune the threshold per platform policy.
Knowledge distillation into a 4–6 layer student, then quantize it, to cut latency and size further.
Use the conversation context (previous messages) and mask only the offensive span.
